title: Randomized execution unfolds to deterministic execution
statement: Let $p$ be a public-coin finite-message protocol over shared-randomness space $\Omega$, private input sets $X$ and $Y$, and output type $\alpha$, and let $x \in X$, $y \in Y$, and $\omega \in \Omega$. Then the randomized execution of $p$ on inputs $x$ and $y$ with shared randomness $\omega$ agrees with the deterministic execution of $p$ on Alice's effective input $(\omega, x)$ and Bob's effective input $(\omega, y)$: \[ \mathrm{rrun}(p, x, y, \omega) = \mathrm{run}(p, (\omega, x), (\omega, y)). \]
hypotheses_covered: p is a public-coin finite-message protocol over Ω, X, Y, α
x is a private input in X
y is a private input in Y
ω is shared randomness in Ω
replaced:
For any protocol $p$, inputs $x$, $y$, and shared randomness $\omega$,
$p.\mathrm{rrun}\,x\,y\,\omega = p.\mathrm{run}\,(\omega, x)\,(\omega, y)$.
This is a definitional unfolding used as a simp lemma.
